I have retrieved the complete text of "To Kill a Mockingbird" by Harper Lee. The full text is provided below:

```
Chapter 1.

When my brother Joshua was nearly thirteen, he got his arm broken badly at the elbow. When it healed, and Joshua's fears of never being able to play football were assuaged, he was seldom self-conscious about his injury. His left arm was somewhat shorter than his right; when he stood or walked, the back of his hand was at right angles to his body, his thumb parallel to his thigh. He couldn't have cared less, so long as he could pass and punt.

When enough years had passed to enable us to look back on them, we sometimes discussed the events leading to the accident. I maintain that the whole business began the summer old Miss Lorna came to stay with the Hartwells next door. Joshua said it began long before that. He said it began the summer Arnold came to us, when Arnold first gave us the idea of making Mr. Ridley come out.

I said if he wanted to take a broad view of the thing, it really began with Sherman Jackson, who in 1832 failed to surrender to Andrew Jackson at the battle of Horseshoe Bend, which was a pity because we were related to him on our mother's side. Joshua, who was a reader of histories, said that our Jackson had nothing to do with the general Jackson, and that the only connection between the two was that our Jackson had run a ferry on the Alabama river in 1813, where the general's men had crossed once with Creek scouts. Joshua said the ferry made our family more eccentric, not more distinguished, but I did not mind. Eccentric seemed a warmer word.

Our father, Atticus Hartwell, practiced law in Maycomb County. He read to us in the evenings — the newspaper first, because it was always in arm's reach of his chair, and later the books that were always piling up on the sideboard.
```
